reason: Color tokens are declared once as light-dark(light, dark) in tokens/schemes.css. getPropertyValue() returns the unresolved light-dark(...) text, alone or inside a composite value such as a box-shadow, where 2.1.1 returned the per-scheme literal. 85 tokens carry it: the 57 written with light-dark(), the tokens defined from them with var() (for example --femto-primary-hover-underline, --femto-card-box-shadow and the two --femto-group-box-shadow-focus-with-* tokens in tokens/base.css), and the generic --femto-background-color, --femto-color, --femto-border-color, --femto-box-shadow and --femto-underline that later modules set from them on elements. What the tokens resolve to is compared separately (kind token) and matches, except tokens-group-island-focus-ring.
notes: Narrowed in Phase 1 from the broad seed (/^--femto-/) to the 84 names a hybrid run of Styles, Color schemes and Document over every default page, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, reported (run p1-enum-1, 2026-10-27). Every reported femto value contained light-dark(. --femto-underline was added after review round 3: it is probed only at anchors on links that carry data-theme, and tokens-schemes.html gained two such links then (run orch-narrow-check, 2026-10-28).

reason: 2.1.1 builds the two group focus-ring tokens on :root, :host from var(--femto-primary-focus) and var(--femto-form-element-border-color), so the value is fixed in the root's scheme and a nested data-theme island, or an element carrying data-theme itself, inherits the page's ring color. With light-dark() the token keeps the pair and resolves per element, so inside an island whose scheme differs from the page the ring takes the island's color. Only the box-shadow probe resolves these tokens.
notes: Was group-island-focus-ring-tokens in components-group.json (seed from PLAN and spike 05). Narrowed in Phase 1: the seed's selector (div[data-theme], div[data-theme] *) missed elements that carry data-theme themselves (article, button, details, section, span, input) and dialogs and cards inside islands; the root is excluded because a data-theme on html changes the root's own scheme, where both sides agree. Review round 2 pinned both values to the single-ring shape the tokens resolve to (a color, three zero offsets and a spread in px), so a missing or doubled ring, or a ring with offsets, is no longer registered.

reason: light-dark() follows the used color-scheme of the element it resolves on, and an author may set color-scheme on any element. In 2.1.1 such an element without data-theme switched only the browser's own colors (scrollbars, native control parts, system colors) while Pico's tokens stayed the per-scheme literals of the root's or the nearest data-theme's scheme, so the subtree mixed two schemes. In femto the tokens resolve to the author's scheme too, so text, backgrounds, borders, outlines, accent and placeholder colors switch with it. The simpler light-dark() conversion fixes the mismatch; use data-theme to theme a subtree as in 2.1.1.
notes: Found in Phase 1's review. Fixture: div#cs-dark in tokens-schemes.html, an inline color-scheme: dark on a light page. Chrome and Firefox report only these color longhands, on the element and its ::placeholder. Review round 2 moved it from new-token, which PLAN reserves for tokens that replace Sass arithmetic or a compile-time branch, to natural-fix, as PLAN classes the island focus ring, the other rendered consequence of light-dark().

reason: Same mechanism as tokens-author-color-scheme-dark, the other way: an inline color-scheme: light on a dark page resolves femto's tokens light there, matching the browser's own light colors in that subtree, where 2.1.1 kept the page's dark literals.
notes: Found in Phase 1's review. Fixture: div#cs-light in tokens-schemes.html. Moved to natural-fix in review round 2; see tokens-author-color-scheme-dark.

selector: :is(a, button, input, select, textarea, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, [role=button], [role=link])[data-theme]:not(:root), :is(a, button, input, select, textarea, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, [role=button], [role=link])[data-theme]:not(:root) *
reason: Decision 12: color tokens are declared once on :root, :host and data-theme only sets color-scheme. 2.1.1 redeclared every color token on each [data-theme] element at specificity (0,1,0), which overrode an element's own lower-specificity token rules (a, button, input, select, textarea and h1 to h6 set --femto-color, --femto-background-color or --femto-box-shadow at (0,0,0) or (0,0,1)) and recomputed derived tokens such as --femto-code-kbd-color: var(--femto-background-color) from the page's colors on that element. So on a dark page <button data-theme=light> was a page-colored box while <input type=submit data-theme=light>, whose [type=submit] rule wins at (0,1,0), was a normal button. In femto an element that carries data-theme itself keeps its own color tokens in its scheme, so both are normal light buttons. The simpler conversion fixes the inconsistency. Rendered colors and box-shadows of such an element and what inherits from it change.
notes: Seed from PLAN (Decision 12), added in Phase 1's review round 2. The selector lists the elements whose 2.1.1 rules set scheme tokens on themselves at a specificity that loses to [data-theme], carrying data-theme, plus their descendants, which inherit the element's tokens (the option of a dark select differs). Narrowed after review round 3 (F1) to what a hybrid run of tokens-schemes.html at 1280, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, with the three tokens-own-data-theme entries removed reported (runs orch-no-own3 and orch-no-own4, 2026-10-28): color longhands, background-color and box-shadow, in the base and focus states, only on this page. summary was dropped from the list: a summary carrying data-theme shows no difference. Fixtures: button[data-theme=dark], button.contrast[data-theme=light], input[type=submit][data-theme=dark], input[name=own-dark], input[name=own-dark-check], select[name=own-dark-select], textarea[name=own-dark-textarea], h1[data-theme=dark], a[data-theme=dark], a.secondary[data-theme=light] and span[role=button][data-theme=dark] in tokens-schemes.html.

reason: Same cause as tokens-own-data-theme-style (Decision 12): at an anchor that carries data-theme itself, the element's own token rules and the tokens derived from them resolve as in the element's own rules, not from 2.1.1's redeclared page colors. This includes elements such as input[type=submit] whose own rules already won in 2.1.1, where only derived tokens like --femto-range-thumb-border-color: var(--femto-background-color) differ.
notes: Seed from PLAN (Decision 12), added in Phase 1's review round 2; see tokens-own-data-theme-style. Narrowed after review round 3 (F1) to what a hybrid run of tokens-schemes.html at 1280, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, with the three tokens-own-data-theme entries removed reported (runs orch-no-own3 and orch-no-own4, 2026-10-28): these 11 tokens.

reason: Same cause as tokens-own-data-theme-style (Decision 12): the raw text of a token at an anchor that carries data-theme itself is the element's own rule (for example #0172ad from button's var(--femto-primary-background)) where 2.1.1 had the redeclared page literal.
notes: Seed from PLAN (Decision 12), added in Phase 1's review round 2; see tokens-own-data-theme-style. The femto pattern leaves values containing light-dark( to tokens-light-dark-raw-text, so this entry covers only raw text that comes from the element's own rules. Narrowed after review round 3 (F1) to what a hybrid run of tokens-schemes.html at 1280, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, with the three tokens-own-data-theme entries removed reported (runs orch-no-own3 and orch-no-own4, 2026-10-28): these three tokens; --femto-underline's raw text on links carrying data-theme is light-dark() text, covered by tokens-light-dark-raw-text.

reason: 2.1.1 set --femto-form-element-focus-color: var(--femto-primary-focus) on button-like inputs, checkboxes, radios and file inputs in three rules, one under each scheme selector ([data-theme=light] input, :root:not([data-theme=dark]) input, :host(:not([data-theme=dark])) input, and the two dark ones), all with the same value. Inside a shadow root whose host carries data-theme=dark, none of them match: the host is reachable only through :host(), and 2.1.1 has no :host([data-theme=dark]) rule. So those inputs kept the root value var(--femto-primary-border) and drew a solid primary ring on focus where every other checkbox and radio draws the translucent primary-focus ring. With light-dark() the per-scheme copies are identical, so femto writes one flat input:is(...) rule, which also covers these inputs (Decisions 3 and 12: data-theme only sets color-scheme).
notes: Found in Phase 1's review round 3 (R3T-1, R3T-2, F3). Fixtures: the shadow-dark-host-c1 checkbox and shadow-dark-host-r radio in tokens-schemes.html, which carry data-states="focus" for this. The light host's inputs matched :host(:not([data-theme=dark])) in 2.1.1 and do not differ. :host() in Element.matches() inside a shadow tree is checked in Chrome and Firefox; Safari is first checked at the Phase 4 gate.

reason: Decision 12: a shadow host carrying data-theme=dark is dark. 2.1.1's forced-dark rules use only [data-theme=dark], which a stylesheet inside a shadow root cannot match on its host, so a contrast accordion summary or busy contrast button in such a shadow root kept the light icon filter. femto adds :host([data-theme=dark]) to the forced-dark rules, as 2.1.1 already has :host(:not([data-theme=dark])) for light hosts, so those icons take the dark filter brightness(0). Like 2.1.1's [data-theme=dark] descendant rules on the page, this also reaches a data-theme=light island inside that shadow root: in 2.1.1 a contrast summary in a light island nested in a dark element already gets brightness(0).
notes: Owner decision 2026-10-28, recorded under Decision 12 in PLAN. Fixtures: the contrast summary and busy contrast button directly in the shadow-dark-host template of tokens-schemes.html and in its inner light island (run orch-darkhost-probe). The case it is for, femto loaded only inside the shadow root of a dark host, cannot be a harness fixture because every fixture page loads the stylesheet in the outer document; the standalone check in the Phase 1 notes covers it. 2.1.1 gave such a host no color tokens at all.

reason: A user stylesheet with ':root { --femto-primary: ... }' now takes effect everywhere. In 2.1.1 it took effect only on a root carrying data-theme=dark, whose [data-theme=dark] block is (0,1,0) like the user's :root. Otherwise it lost to the light block's ':root:not([data-theme=dark])' or the media-dark block's ':root:not([data-theme])' at (0,2,0), and every [data-theme] element redeclared the tokens, undoing it inside islands. femto declares the color tokens once on ':root, :host' (Decision 12), where :root is (0,1,0), so a later :root rule wins on the root and inherits into data-theme islands, which only switch color-scheme.
notes: Seed from PLAN. Applies only to a comparison preset named user-root-override that loads a user override stylesheet after both sides; no such preset exists yet.

reason: Same cause as tokens-root-user-override-style: the user's :root override of the primary tokens now wins on the root and inherits into data-theme islands, so the tokens resolve to the user's values there.

--femto-primary-inverse-filter replaces a compile-time @if in _styles.scss, which picked the loading-spinner filter on filled buttons by comparing the theme's primary-inverse to white: brightness(0) invert(1) for the 14 white-inverse themes, brightness(0) invert(0) for amber, grey, lime, pumpkin, sand and yellow. tokens/base.css declares it on :root, :host, where 2.1.1's literal applied (every root and shadow host, whatever its scheme), and theme files override it there; the computed filter is unchanged.
notes: Narrowed in Phase 1 from the seed's four names. --femto-box-shadow-color was not needed: the seven box-shadow layers are written as light-dark() pairs of the compiled colors. --femto-switch-width and --femto-switch-height belong to forms/checkbox-radio-switch (Phase 2), which registers them if it adds them.
